paras: The Caldwell jail lynching was the shooting of Mexican prisoners in the jail at Caldwell, Texas, by a mob on the night of January 14 or 15, 1888. The prisoners were held on a charge of murdering a local planter, and at least one of them was killed. The Fort Worth Gazette reported one man dead and another dangerously wounded, while a Galveston wire and later news briefs spread the story nationally as the lynching of "two Mexican murderers."

About ten days before the attack, a man the Gazette called "old man Alford" was killed near Caldwell, and three Mexicans were jailed for the crime. Wire reports described him as a planter, spelling the name Alford or Alvord. According to the Gazette's Caldwell correspondent, one of the prisoners, Mat Pettis, confessed on Saturday evening that he had done the killing with the help of another Mexican named Reto. The wire version named the prisoner who confessed as Pazo.

At about 8:30 that Saturday night, by the Gazette's account, a mob of forty or fifty people came to the jail and demanded admission from the guards. The mob went in through the front door and a wooden partition to the run-around of the cages, where the accused men were held with a third Mexican and a Black prisoner. Shooting began at once, and when the sheriff and others entered after the mob had gone, they found the man who had confessed dead from four gunshot wounds. The man he had implicated, who had also confessed, was dangerously wounded, while the third Mexican and the Black prisoner were unhurt.

The Galveston News special told it differently: the mob ordered the Black cellmate to throw the Mexicans out of the cell one by one. After what it called "a terrible struggle," he pushed out Pazo and another Mexican, both of whom were shot before the mob left.
No report of an inquest, of arrests of mob members, or of the fate of the wounded prisoner appears in the coverage.

The fullest account was a special to the Fort Worth Gazette dated at Caldwell on January 16, printed under the head "One Mexican Lynched and Another Dangerously Wounded." The shorter Galveston wire ran the next day as far away as Nevada and Minnesota, and in German in the Chicago Illinois Staats-Zeitung. Kentucky and Ohio papers printed a January 18 version of the wire under "Threw the Mexicans Out to the Mob."

Headlines treated the prisoners' guilt as settled, with the Silver State listing "Two Mexican Murderers Lynched in Texas" and "Two Murderers Taken From Jail and Shot." By late January the story had shrunk to a single line in roundup columns in Rhode Island and South Carolina, which said the two had been "shot dead by lynchers." None of these reports criticized the mob.

The reports disagree on the death toll: the Gazette gave one dead and one wounded, the wire said only that both men were shot, and the later briefs called both dead. The Gazette's local account, which describes what the sheriff found after the mob left, is the most detailed. The night also differs, Saturday in the Gazette and Sunday in the Galveston News special, and the man who confessed is named Mat Pettis in one and Pazo in the other.

reader.title: Caldwell jail lynching (1888)
bases: An armed mob forced its way into the Caldwell jail and shot Mexican prisoners held on a murder charge (A1, A3, A6).

A mob of forty or fifty entered the jail and shot dead at least one prisoner held for the murder of a planter, without any lawful authority, to punish the alleged killers (A1, A3); whether one or two died is disputed (A1 vs A8, A9).

The Fort Worth Gazette's Caldwell special (A1) and the separate Galveston News special carried by wire (A3, A6) agree that a mob entered the jail and shot the Mexican prisoners, though they differ on the night, the names and the number killed.

accounts.label: Caldwell special to the Fort Worth Gazette
accounts.gist: Saturday night a mob of forty or fifty demanded entry, went in and fired into the cage; the confessed killer Pettis was found dead, his confessed accomplice dangerously wounded.

accounts.label: Caldwell special to the Galveston News, by wire
accounts.gist: On Sunday night (or 'last night') the mob made a Black cellmate throw the Mexicans out of the cell one by one; Pazo and another Mexican were shot.

accounts.label: News roundup briefs
accounts.gist: Two Mexican murderers in the Caldwell jail were shot dead by lynchers.

framing.detail: The Gazette headed its report 'One Mexican Lynched and Another Dangerously Wounded' and told it as a plain sequence of confession, mob entry and shooting.
Out-of-state papers ran the Galveston wire under heads such as 'Two Murderers Taken From Jail and Shot' and 'Threw the Mexicans Out to the Mob,' calling the prisoners 'the murderers' outright.
Roundup columns in Rhode Island and South Carolina reduced it to one line calling the victims 'Two Mexican murderers'.

conflicts.note: The Gazette's Caldwell special is the most detailed account and reports what the sheriff found after the mob left; the wire says only that both were shot, and the later one-line briefs appear to have read that as two deaths.
